title: Grade 4 SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — Mock Exam #10

pages.quiz:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — MOCK EXAM #10
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which sign of life is shown when a yellow leaf falls from a tree? (1 mark)
   A. Reproducing
   B. Breathing in
   C. Making fruit
   D. Removing waste

2. What do roots of cassava and sweet potato do besides taking in water? (1 mark)
   A. Carry seeds
   B. Make leaves
   C. Make flowers
   D. Store food

3. Which of these is a sign of life in plants? (1 mark)
   A. Walking to find water
   B. Changing into a stone
   C. Growing taller over time
   D. Making a loud noise

4. A pupil finds a small animal under a stone. It has a long soft body, no legs and no shell. It is probably (1 mark)
   A. A frog
   B. An earthworm
   C. A lizard
   D. A snake

5. A goat lifts its head when it hears a noise. Which sign of life is this? (1 mark)
   A. Breathing out
   B. Responding to changes
   C. Reproducing
   D. Growing

6. Which of these statements is true? (1 mark)
   A. All animals can fly
   B. All small animals are insects
   C. All animals have six legs
   D. All fish have a backbone

7. Which of these is a difference between plants and animals? (1 mark)
   A. Plants die but animals do not
   B. Animals do not grow
   C. Plants breathe and animals do not
   D. Animals move from place to place and take in ready-made food

8. Ostrich and flamingo belong to which group? (1 mark)
   A. Birds
   B. Amphibians
   C. Mammals
   D. Reptiles

9. Which of these is a balanced meal? (1 mark)
   A. Ugali, vegetables and beans
   B. Only sweets
   C. Only soda
   D. Only tea

10. What can help a child with diarrhoea while waiting to see a health worker? (1 mark)
   A. Drinking clean water and ORS as advised
   B. Eating only sweets
   C. Eating unwashed fruit
   D. Drinking dirty water

11. Which of these is true of a solid? (1 mark)
   A. It keeps its shape wherever it is put
   B. It has no mass
   C. It takes the shape of any container
   D. It cannot be measured

12. What instrument measures the mass of an object? (1 mark)
   A. Thermometer
   B. Clock
   C. Measuring jug
   D. Balance

13. What instrument measures the volume of a liquid? (1 mark)
   A. Ruler
   B. Stopwatch
   C. Measuring jug
   D. Beam balance

14. A bag has 1 kg of rice and 250 g of beans. What is the total mass? (1 mark)
   A. 1250 g
   B. 2500 g
   C. 350 g
   D. 1025 g

15. In the dry tissue experiment, why does the tissue stay dry? (1 mark)
   A. Water cannot touch paper
   B. The tissue is warm
   C. The cup is made of plastic
   D. Air in the cup keeps the water out

16. Which of these is solid waste? (1 mark)
   A. Dirty bath water
   B. A banana peel
   C. Smoke
   D. Steam

17. Which item is a paper waste that can be recycled? (1 mark)
   A. Old newspapers
   B. Plastic bottle
   C. Glass bottle
   D. Banana peel

18. Which of these is a result of wasting water? (1 mark)
   A. Less money spent
   B. More rain
   C. Less water for others
   D. More trees

19. A school wastes 20 litres a day through leaks. How much in 5 days? (1 mark)
   A. 15 litres
   B. 25 litres
   C. 100 litres
   D. 4 litres

20. What is a force? (1 mark)
   A. A kind of light
   B. A kind of sound
   C. A push or a pull
   D. A kind of matter

21. Where are ball bearings found? (1 mark)
   A. In a book
   B. In a cup
   C. In bicycle wheels
   D. In a pencil

22. Which force pulls objects down towards the Earth? (1 mark)
   A. Sound
   B. Gravity
   C. Friction
   D. Wind

23. What happens to light when it hits an opaque object? (1 mark)
   A. It becomes heat only
   B. It is blocked
   C. It passes through completely
   D. It becomes sound

24. Which of these is a natural source of light at night? (1 mark)
   A. A torch
   B. Stars
   C. A candle
   D. A street lamp

25. Which of these uses sunlight to dry things? (1 mark)
   A. Making ice
   B. Drying clothes and grain
   C. Making stones
   D. Making rain only

26. The moon shines brightly at night. Why is it still not a source of light? (1 mark)
   A. It is too near
   B. It is too small
   C. It reflects light from the sun
   D. It is cold

27. Which of these is opaque? (1 mark)
   A. Clean water
   B. Wood
   C. Clear glass
   D. Clear plastic

28. Why do houses have windows? (1 mark)
   A. To let in only rain
   B. To keep out light
   C. To let in daylight
   D. To make noise

29. Which of these uses heat to change dough into bread? (1 mark)
   A. Freezing
   B. Baking
   C. Cutting
   D. Washing

30. Why should kitchen gloves be dry? (1 mark)
   A. Wet cloth is thicker
   B. Dry cloth is heavier
   C. Dry cloth is colder
   D. Wet cloth passes heat quickly

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. What happens in the large intestine? (2 marks)

32. Explain why we should wash our hands before eating and after using the toilet. (3 marks)

33. Why is it wrong to say that a tree is not alive because it cannot walk? (3 marks)

34. Explain how a pupil can show that plants respond to light. (4 marks)

35. Describe an activity that shows the uses of heat, for example drying clothes in different conditions. (5 marks)

36. Give two examples of decomposable waste and two of non-decomposable waste. (2 marks)

37. Describe what you would put in a portfolio about vertebrates and invertebrates. (4 marks)

38. Sort into decomposable and non-decomposable: egg shells, tin can, cotton cloth, polythene bag, cow dung, glass bottle. (4 marks)

39. Write three ways of managing waste in the classroom. (3 marks)

40. A family of five uses a tap that drips 1 litre every hour. Calculate how much water is wasted in one week and suggest what they should do. (5 marks)

41. State any four signs of life in animals. (2 marks)

42. Explain why we should care for animals and describe how it can be done at home and at school. (5 marks)

43. Describe how you would show that light travels in a straight line. (3 marks)

44. Why do we use kitchen gloves when holding hot pots? (2 marks)

45. Describe what happens to food in the stomach. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — MOCK EXAM #10 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — Removing waste
   Old leaves may carry waste away when they fall.

2. D — Store food
   These roots store food for the plant.

3. C — Growing taller over time
   Plants grow, reproduce, remove waste, respond and die. They do not walk or make noise.

4. B — An earthworm
   An earthworm is a soft, legless invertebrate.

5. B — Responding to changes
   The goat responds to a change in its surroundings, a sound.

6. D — All fish have a backbone
   Fish are vertebrates. Small animals may be spiders, worms or others.

7. D — Animals move from place to place and take in ready-made food
   Most animals move about and eat food, while plants make their own food.

8. A — Birds
   Both have feathers and lay eggs.

9. A — Ugali, vegetables and beans
   A balanced meal has energy foods, body-building foods and protective foods.

10. A — Drinking clean water and ORS as advised
   Water and ORS replace what the body loses.

11. A — It keeps its shape wherever it is put
   A solid has a definite shape.

12. D — Balance
   A balance is used to measure mass.

13. C — Measuring jug
   A measuring jug or cylinder shows volume.

14. A — 1250 g
   1 kg = 1000 g, and 1000 + 250 = 1250 g.

15. D — Air in the cup keeps the water out
   Air takes up the space inside the cup.

16. B — A banana peel
   A banana peel is a solid thrown away.

17. A — Old newspapers
   Paper can be turned into new paper.

18. C — Less water for others
   Wasted water is not available to others.

19. C — 100 litres
   20 x 5 = 100 litres.

20. C — A push or a pull
   A force is a push or a pull.

21. C — In bicycle wheels
   Bicycle wheels use ball bearings.

22. B — Gravity
   Gravity pulls things towards the centre of the Earth.

23. B — It is blocked
   Opaque objects do not let light pass.

24. B — Stars
   Stars give out their own light.

25. B — Drying clothes and grain
   Sunlight dries wet things.

26. C — It reflects light from the sun
   The moon does not make its own light.

27. B — Wood
   Wood blocks light.

28. C — To let in daylight
   Windows allow sunlight to enter the room.

29. B — Baking
   Baking uses heat.

30. D — Wet cloth passes heat quickly
   Wet cloth can burn your hand.

SECTION B
----
31. (2 marks)
   Answer: Water is taken back from the leftover food and the rest becomes faeces.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for water and 1 mark for faeces.

32. (3 marks)
   Answer: Hands may carry germs and worm eggs. Washing removes them and stops them entering the mouth and causing disease.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for germs on hands, 1 mark for washing removes them, 1 mark for preventing illness.

33. (3 marks)
   Answer: Plants show life in other ways. They grow, reproduce, respond, remove waste and die. Only some animals walk.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for stating plants show signs of life, 1 mark for naming signs, 1 mark for saying walking is not a sign needed for all living things.

34. (4 marks)
   Answer: Put a plant in a box with a hole on one side. After some days the plant bends towards the hole showing it responds to light.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the set up, 1 mark for the hole giving light from one side, 1 mark for the plant bending, 1 mark for conclusion.

35. (5 marks)
   Answer: Wet two similar cloths. Hang one in the sun and the other in the shade. After some time, feel them. The cloth in the sun dries faster because heat from the sun evaporates the water.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for materials, 1 mark for method, 1 mark for fair comparison, 1 mark for observation, 1 mark for conclusion.

36. (2 marks)
   Answer: Decomposable: vegetable peelings, dung, leaves. Non-decomposable: plastic, tin, glass.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct pair.

37. (4 marks)
   Answer: A drawing of each animal, its name, whether it is a vertebrate or invertebrate, one sign of life seen, put together in a folder.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four items.

38. (4 marks)
   Answer: Decomposable: egg shells, cotton cloth, cow dung. Non-decomposable: tin can, polythene bag, glass bottle.
   Working / marking points: Award 4 marks for all correct, 3 for five, 2 for four and 1 for three.

39. (3 marks)
   Answer: Use a bin with a lid, put paper in a separate box for reusing, do not litter, make monitors.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

40. (5 marks)
   Answer: 24 x 7 = 168 litres. They should repair the tap or ask an adult or plumber to fix it.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 24 hours, 1 mark for 24 x 7, 1 mark for 168, 1 mark for fixing the tap, 1 mark for units.

41. (2 marks)
   Answer: Feeding, growing, breathing, reproducing, removing waste, moving, responding to changes, dying (any four).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for two correct signs and 2 marks for four.

42. (5 marks)
   Answer: Animals give us milk, meat, eggs and honey and help us in work. They are part of nature. We give them food, water, shelter and medical care and we do not hurt them. At school we keep the compound safe for birds.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for reasons and 3 marks for ways.

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: Use three cards with holes in the middle and line them up in a row. Shine a torch through the holes. Light passes. Move the middle card and the light is blocked.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for set up, 1 mark for observation and 1 mark for conclusion.

44. (2 marks)
   Answer: Gloves are poor passers of heat so they protect hands from burns.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for poor at passing heat and 1 mark for protection from burns.

45. (3 marks)
   Answer: The stomach churns the food and mixes it with strong juices. The juices kill many germs and break down the food into a thick soup.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for churns, 1 mark for juices and 1 mark for germs or thick soup.
